sara_sales: Hi team — large enterprise (financial services) evaluating Redwood Private. They need an air-gapped POC and have two hard constraints: no outbound egress from the site, and a 30-day freeze period after initial install where no upgrades are allowed. Pricing team asking about annual pricing uplift for that model.

sara_sales: Asking: can we support a signed minibundle/USB workflow that allows security to vet artifacts locally, and what are the risks/constraints for upgrades after the 30-day freeze?

devon_se: Short answer: yes, but there are tradeoffs. We can produce signed minibundles + a sidecar operator for offline install. Main risks: CVE patch lag during freeze, and operator compatibility if cluster runtime changes.

devon_se: Two paths: (1) full immutable image (single-file) — simpler to validate but heavy bandwidth for airgap transfer; (2) chunked minibundles with signed deltas — much smaller transfers but needs a deterministic apply ordering and a small bootstrap verifier.

eli_ops: we did a similar flow for a telco POC. Suggest: initial install = full signed bundle; subsequent hotfixes = signed delta chunks. For 30-day freeze we can tag the install as "frozen: true" in the metadata and block auto-upgrade paths.

eli_ops: Example manifest snippet we hand off to customers for validation:

```
manifest_version: 1
image: redwood-private-1.20.3.tar.gz
signatures:
  - signer: redwood-notary
    sig: <BASE64>
frozen: true
chunks: ["core.tar.gz", "gpu-kernel.tar.gz"]
```

maya_legal: Security questionnaire Q: will the bundle include any telemetry/phone-home components by default? Customer requires zero outbound unless explicitly enabled from their console.

devon_se: By default Private builds have telemetry disabled in air-gapped configs. We ship an opt-in telemetry agent that is disabled in the signed minibundle. We can provide an SBOM and a build provenance chain (notary signatures).

maya_legal: Also need KMS/HSM workflow doc for license activation and bundle signing — customer requires proof of HSM-backed signing or allowlist of our signing key fingerprints.

ron_pm: Commercial side — we can offer a one-time airgap packaging fee plus an annual uplift for on-site support and extended cold-hotfix SLA. For a 30-day freeze with signed bundles and HSM attestation the uplift is typically +20-30% on top of Private license. Will fine-tune with finance.

ron_pm: Two commercial levers: (A) packaging labor (one-time), (B) airgap support plan (annual). Proposal: packaging fee covers signed bundle generation, offline verification script, and customer handoff package.

ci-build-bot: build 6823141601: signed-bundle-redwood-1.20.3.tar.gz ready -> SHA256: d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e

sara_sales: Nice. Customer also worried about upgrade cadence after freeze. If they freeze for 30 days, can we support a safe path to re-enable upgrades?

devon_se: Yes — two mechanisms: (1) manual revalidation by ops (customer runs a local verifier script that checks signatures and hashes and flips frozen:false); (2) allowlist workflow — they register approved bundle fingerprints with the private control plane via an offline signed token. Both are customer-facing ops steps.

eli_ops: Operational notes: if they stay frozen for longer than 90 days, we recommend a compatibility check window — some kernel/runtime changes require a rebase. We can produce a compatibility report as part of the handoff.

maya_legal: Addendum: need to ship legal T&Cs for offline licensing, indemnities for delayed patching during freeze, and a clear escalation matrix for security-critical fixes.

ron_pm: I'll draft a commercial letter with 3 options (standard, airgap-basic, airgap-premium). Sara — can you collect customer target metrics (max USB transfer size per window, expected frequency of hotfixes) so we can size packaging and pricing?

sara_sales: Will ask them today. Also they want an install checklist to share with their security team. Can we produce a one-page runbook?

devon_se: Yes — I'll attach a 1-pager runbook snippet to the POC artifact. It will include: preflight checks, offline signature verification command, bootstrap sequence, and rollback steps.

eli_ops: Rollback note: with chunked minibundles we support chunk-level rollback but only if your operator has the previous chunks cached. Recommend keeping the previous full bundle for 30 days as rollback fall-back.

sara_sales: Great — thanks everyone. I'll pull pricing targets and customer constraints, and post back with their acceptance criteria and transfer window size. :thumbsup:
